contact.title: New Contact
contact.fullDescription: Creates a contact record in the CRM. Useful to capture lead information coming from forms, imports or manual entries.
contact.configureDescription: Create or update a contact; map required fields and dedupe.
contact.how: Use this node to create or update a contact. Map incoming fields (name, email, phone) and set deduplication rules.
examples: Create contact when a form is submitted
Update contact when an incoming webhook provides an email

offer.title: Create Offer
offer.fullDescription: Generates a commercial offer document (PDF) using selected items and pricing rules.
offer.configureDescription: Generate an offer from selected items and pricing rules.
offer.how: Select items and pricing, then render an offer. You can attach the generated offer to a contact or send it by email.
examples: Auto-generate an offer after a pricing approval
Create offer when a sales rep selects items

email.title: Email
email.fullDescription: Sends an email based on a template or free text. Supports attachments and recipient selection.
email.configureDescription: Choose template, recipients and timing for the email.
email.how: Choose a template, set recipients and timing. Use variables to personalize the content.
examples: Send welcome email to new contact
Send invoice when sale is confirmed

sale.title: Sale
sale.fullDescription: Creates a sale record from an offer or other source. Handles financial details, customer assignment, and can trigger invoicing or inventory reservation.
sale.configureDescription: Map offer fields to create a sale and choose invoicing/stock behavior.
sale.how: Map the offer fields (items, prices, customer) and configure whether to automatically generate an invoice or reserve stock. Use this node after an offer is accepted or when auto-converting quotes.
examples: Convert an accepted offer into a sale and send invoice
Automatically create a sale when an offer reaches 'accepted' status
Reserve stock and notify warehouse upon sale creation

dispatch.title: Dispatch
dispatch.fullDescription: Creates or updates a dispatch entry to assign field technicians, schedule jobs, and track the status of service tasks. Integrates with calendar and map views for planning and routing.
dispatch.configureDescription: Create or update dispatches; configure assignment rules and notifications.
dispatch.how: Map the source data (service order, customer, address, time window) to create a dispatch. Configure technician assignment rules, priority, and notifications. Use this node when a service needs scheduling or when an order requires field execution.
examples: Create a dispatch when a service order is confirmed
Assign technician automatically based on skills and availability
Update dispatch status and notify the customer when technician is en route

loop.title: Loop
loop.fullDescription: Repeats a set of actions either for a fixed number of iterations or while a condition holds true. Useful for processing lists or retrying operations.
loop.configureDescription: Process items or retry operations; configure iteration mode and max attempts.
loop.how: Configure the iteration mode (count or condition), map the loop body actions, and set termination rules or maximum iterations. Use loops to process arrays, retry transient failures, or perform batch operations.
examples: Process each item in an invoice's items list
Retry an API call up to 3 times until it succeeds
Iterate over customer subscriptions to apply a billing update

service-order.title: Service Order
service-order.fullDescription: Creates or schedules a service order to manage field operations, tasks, and customer requests.
service-order.how: Map customer, items and preferred time windows to create a service order. Configure technicians, priorities and notifications for execution.
examples: Create a service order when a customer requests an installation
Schedule maintenance visits automatically based on contract terms

email-template.title: Email Template
email-template.fullDescription: Sends an email using a selected template, with variables and attachments support.
email-template.how: Select a template, map variables and choose recipients. Useful for standardized communications like invoices or confirmations.
examples: Send invoice email using the invoice template
Send appointment confirmation using a template

email-llm.title: AI Email
email-llm.fullDescription: Generates personalized email content using an LLM model and sends it to recipients.
email-llm.how: Provide a prompt or template and let the model generate the email body. Review or auto-send based on workflow rules.
examples: Generate a personalized outreach email for a lead
Create a follow-up message based on recent activity

llm-writer.title: AI Writer
llm-writer.fullDescription: Generates text content using a language model for emails, descriptions, or other text fields.
llm-writer.how: Provide a prompt and parameters (tone, length). The model will generate content which you can review or send automatically.
examples: Generate an email follow-up for a lead
Create a product description from item details

llm-analyzer.title: AI Analyzer
llm-analyzer.fullDescription: Analyzes text or data using an AI model to extract insights, summaries, or classifications.
llm-analyzer.how: Feed data or text to the analyzer and configure the output type (summary, tags, sentiment). Use results to drive workflow decisions.
examples: Summarize customer feedback
Classify support tickets by topic

llm-personalizer.title: AI Personalizer
llm-personalizer.fullDescription: Personalizes messages or content per recipient using AI-driven data and templates.
llm-personalizer.how: Provide recipient data and a template; the personalizer fills variables and adapts tone or content for each recipient.
examples: Personalize email body with customer details
Adjust marketing copy by segment

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.fullDescription: Starts the workflow based on a manual action, event, or schedule.
trigger.how: Choose how the workflow should start: manually, via webhook, scheduled or based on external events.
examples: Run workflow manually from UI
Start workflow when a new order is created

webhook.title: Webhook
webhook.fullDescription: Starts or interacts with the workflow when an external system sends an HTTP request.
webhook.how: Expose an endpoint or use an existing webhook integration to trigger the workflow and map payload fields to node inputs.
examples: Trigger workflow when payment provider posts a webhook
Receive form submissions via webhook

scheduled.title: Scheduled
scheduled.fullDescription: Runs the workflow on a defined schedule (cron or time-based rules).
scheduled.how: Define cron expressions or time windows to automatically run workflows at specific times or intervals.
examples: Run nightly maintenance workflows
Send weekly summary emails

if-else.title: If / Else
if-else.fullDescription: Evaluates a condition and routes the workflow through two branches: true or false.
if-else.how: Define a condition based on fields or data and configure actions for both true and false paths.
examples: If customer credit > 1000 then approve
If order total is 0 then skip payment step

switch.title: Switch
switch.fullDescription: Routes execution across multiple branches depending on a value.
switch.how: Provide the field to switch on and define cases for each possible value to route the flow.
examples: Route by country to different handlers
Switch based on payment method

parallel.title: Parallel
parallel.fullDescription: Runs multiple branches concurrently and can wait for all or the first to complete.
parallel.how: Configure multiple branches and choose whether to wait for all to finish or proceed on the first completion.
parallel.configureDescription: Run branches concurrently; choose wait-for-all or proceed-on-first.
examples: Run multiple checks in parallel
Fan-out processing of items

try-catch.title: Try / Catch
try-catch.fullDescription: Attempts an action and provides error handling branches on failure.
try-catch.how: Wrap risky operations in try-catch and configure retries, fallback actions or error notifications.
examples: Retry API call on transient failure
Fallback to alternative service on error

action.title: Action
action.fullDescription: Performs a custom action, such as updating records, calling APIs, or running scripts.
action.how: Configure the action type and provide necessary parameters. Use actions to mutate data or trigger side effects.
examples: Update CRM record
Call external API to push data

database.title: Database
database.fullDescription: Performs database operations like create, update, delete or query records.
database.how: Configure the database action, table/collection and field mappings. Use queries to fetch data for decisions.
examples: Insert a record on new lead
Update status after processing

api.title: API
api.fullDescription: Calls external APIs to fetch or push data as part of the workflow.
api.how: Configure endpoint, method, headers and body. Map responses to workflow variables and handle errors.
examples: Call payment gateway to charge card
Fetch product info by Reference

condition.title: Condition
condition.fullDescription: Evaluates a condition to decide workflow routing based on data or fields.
condition.how: Define operators and comparison values. Use condition results to route flow branches.
examples: If customer type is premium then route to priority flow
Check if inventory > 0 before creating a dispatch

filter.title: Filter
filter.fullDescription: Filters items based on criteria to pass only matching items down the flow.
filter.how: Define filter conditions and pass-through settings. Useful to prune lists or events before processing.
examples: Filter orders with total > 100
Filter leads from specific campaigns

demo.title: How to build a workflow
demo.emptyDesc: Start by adding a trigger node to begin your workflow. Drag components from the toolbar and connect them.
demo.emptyHint: Or drag a node from the panel on the left
demo.finished: That's the full tour — Triggers, Actions, Conditions, Approvals, AI, Integrations and Publishing. Click the help button anytime to replay or jump to a chapter.
demo.s1: Welcome. Let's build a workflow together — watch how it's done.
demo.s2: The left palette holds every node type. We start with triggers.
demo.s3: Grab a Status Change trigger from the palette…
demo.s4: …and drop it on the canvas. Triggers are what start a workflow.
demo.s5: Double-click any node to configure it.
demo.s6: Pick the entity (Offer) and the status transition (draft → sent), then save.
demo.s7: Now open the Actions category — that's what the workflow will do.
demo.s9: …and drop it next to the trigger.
demo.s10: Drag from the trigger's right handle to the email's left handle to connect them.
demo.s11: Open Logic and grab a Condition node — to branch the flow.
demo.s12: Drop and connect it. Conditions split the flow into true/false paths.
demo.s13: Add a Send SMS action for the true branch…
demo.s15: And a Notification for the false branch.
demo.s16: Add an Approval node to pause for a human decision (role + timeout).
demo.s17: Approvals wait for a manager — the workflow resumes once they decide.
demo.s18: Click Save to persist your workflow.
demo.s19: Toggle Activate to make it run on real events.
demo.s20: Hit Test run to fire it once and watch each node execute live.
demo.welcome: Welcome. In the next few minutes you'll see exactly what a workflow is, how it runs, and how to build one — no prior knowledge needed.
demo.layout: Layout: the left panel is the Palette (every step you can use), the middle is the Canvas (where you draw the flow), the right opens when you configure a step.
demo.toolbarTour: Top bar: Save snapshots a new version · Activate turns the workflow on for real events · Test runs it once on sample data so you can see the logs.

trig.openCat: Open the Triggers category. Triggers are the only nodes that can start a workflow.
trig.itemList: There are 6 trigger types: status changes on Offer / Sale / Service Order / Dispatch, plus Webhook and Scheduled.
trig.grab: Click + drag the Offer · Status Change trigger from the palette…
trig.drop: …and drop it on the canvas. Every workflow must start with exactly one trigger.
trig.openConfig: Double-click the node to open its configuration panel on the right.
trig.fieldsExplain: Pick the entity (Offer), the From status (draft, or any) and the To status (sent). The trigger fires the moment that transition happens in the app.
trig.save: Click Apply changes to save the trigger config — the node now shows the status pill 'draft → sent'.

act.openCat: Open Communication. This holds Send Email, In-app Notification, Approval, Delay, Human Input Form and Wait for Event.
act.drop: …and drop it next to the trigger.
act.connect: Connect the trigger's right handle to the email's left handle — that's how data flows.
act.openConfig: Open the email config. Every field supports {{ variables }} from previous nodes.
act.variables: Recipient, Subject and Body all accept variables like {{ trigger.contact.email }} or {{ offer.totalAmount }}. Toggle 'Attach PDF of entity' to include the generated PDF.
act.save: Apply changes — the node now summarises its config below the title.

cond.openCat: Open Conditions. If/Else branches the flow, Switch handles many cases, Loop iterates over arrays.
cond.drop: …and drop it below the trigger. It auto-connects from the trigger.
cond.openConfig: Open the config. Pick a Field (any value from previous nodes), an Operator and a Value.
cond.save: Apply changes — the condition now has 'true' and 'false' output handles.
cond.branches: Add a Send SMS on the 'true' branch and an In-app Notification on 'false'. Each branch runs independently.

appr.grab: Grab Request Approval from Communication — it pauses the workflow until a human decides.
appr.drop: Drop it after Send Email. The workflow halts at this node until approval.
appr.openConfig: Configure: approver role (Sales Manager, Operations Lead, Finance, Admin or specific user), timeout in hours, and what happens on timeout (auto-reject / auto-approve / escalate).
appr.save: Apply changes — approvers see this in their 'Pending Approvals' inbox and get an email.

ai.openCat: Open AI. These nodes use Lovable AI Gateway — no API keys needed.
ai.grab: Grab AI · Email Writer to generate personalised email bodies on the fly.
ai.drop: Drop it. AI nodes work like any other action — they can be chained, branched, looped.
ai.openConfig: Pick a model (Gemini Flash is fast & cheap, GPT-5 is most capable), a Tone preset, write your prompt with {{ variables }}, and optionally translate the output.
ai.save: Apply changes — the AI node will run on each trigger event and pass its output to downstream nodes.

int.openCat: Open Integration. HTTP Request calls any external API; Dynamic Form opens a form to a user; Data Transfer copies fields between entities; Custom Code runs sandboxed JavaScript.
int.grab: Grab HTTP Request to push the approved offer to your ERP.
int.openConfig: Choose method, URL, auth scheme. Use {{ secrets.MY_TOKEN }} to inject secrets stored in Settings → Secrets. The response is available downstream as {{ http.response }}.
int.save: Apply changes — secrets are encrypted at rest and never logged.

pub.review: Before publishing — quick visual review. Validate that every branch ends, every async node has a timeout, and no secret is hard-coded.
pub.save: Click Save in the toolbar. This persists a new DRAFT version — it does not run yet.
pub.versioning: Every Save creates a new immutable version. You can roll back, diff two versions, or pin a specific version to a tenant.
pub.activate: Toggle Activate to publish the current draft as the live version.
pub.activeExplain: When active, real events trigger the workflow. Toggling off pauses it instantly — running executions finish their current node and then halt.
pub.test: Test run fires the workflow once with sample data. The execution panel slides up showing each node's status.
pub.logsExplain: Status legend — green: ok · amber: waiting · blue: running · red: failed. Click any node to inspect its input, output, duration, retries and logs.
pub.monitoring: All runs are kept for 30 days under Executions → History, with filters by status, trigger entity, version and user. Failed runs can be retried in one click.
pub.saveIntro: Time to publish. First we Save — this stores the current canvas as a new immutable version.
pub.activateIntro: The workflow is saved but still dormant. To make it react to real events we have to Activate it.
pub.testIntro: Before sending real users into it, let’s do a Test run — sample data, no side effects, full per-node telemetry.

delay.intro: Delay nodes pause the workflow for a duration or until a condition. They are checkpointed — restarts and deploys do not lose state.
delay.drop: Drop it after the AI node — we want to wait before sending a follow-up.
delay.openConfig: Modes: relative duration, absolute date, business hours, or wait-until-field-matches.
delay.advancedTab: Advanced — set a max wait safety cap and how the delay reacts if the upstream entity changes.
delay.save: Apply changes — delays are durable: the workflow sleeps server-side until ready.

loop.intro: Loop iterates over any array and runs its inner branch per item.
loop.drop: Drop it — connect to the trigger to process every offer line.
loop.openConfig: Point Source collection at any array variable. The Item alias is exposed to inner nodes as {{ item }}.
loop.outputs: Sequential keeps order; Parallel is faster but order is not guaranteed. Max iterations is a runaway-guard.
loop.save: Apply changes — the loop node exposes both an inner branch handle and a 'done' handle for after all iterations.

switch.grab: Grab Switch — use it when If/Else has too many branches.
switch.drop: Drop it. Each case becomes its own output handle.
switch.openConfig: Pick the field to switch on, then list cases. 'default' catches anything that doesn't match.
switch.casesExplain: Cases support exact match, regex (/^EU/), or value list (TN,FR,DE). Order matters — first match wins unless Fallthrough is on.
switch.save: Apply changes — every case now has its own handle for chaining.

sched.intro: Scheduled triggers are the workflow's heartbeat — perfect for digests, reminders, and cleanups.
sched.drop: Drop it on the canvas. Scheduled triggers don't need an upstream entity.
sched.openConfig: Pick a frequency preset or write a cron expression. Timezone matters for business hours.
sched.cronExplain: Cron syntax: minute hour day month weekday. '0 9 * * 1' = 09:00 every Monday. Add @hourly / @daily / @weekly shortcuts too.
sched.save: Apply changes — next run timestamp is visible on the node header.

web.grab: Grab Webhook from Triggers — let external systems push events to you.
web.drop: Drop it. A unique signed URL is auto-generated.
web.openConfig: Configure method, auth (HMAC, Bearer, IP allowlist), and how to acknowledge the caller.
web.advanced: Advanced — enable idempotency, rate-limiting and signature verification before processing.
web.save: Apply changes — copy the URL into the source system (Stripe, GitHub, Zapier, etc.).

code.grab: Grab Custom Code from Integration — for transformations beyond what built-in nodes offer.
code.drop: Drop it after HTTP Request to post-process the response.
code.openConfig: Write JavaScript with full access to upstream variables via `ctx`. Return any JSON — it becomes available as {{ code.* }} downstream.
code.save: Apply changes — code runs in a sandbox with 5s timeout and no network by default.

err.intro: Open the HTTP Request node and switch to the Advanced tab to configure resilience.
err.retryExplain: Exponential backoff doubles the wait between retries (2s → 4s → 8s …) up to Max backoff, then alerts.
err.fallback: On final failure you can: stop the whole workflow, mark this node failed and continue, branch into an error-handling path, or call a fallback node.
err.save: Apply changes — retries and failures are recorded in execution logs with full request/response payloads.

var.intro: Every node exposes its output as a namespaced variable, available downstream via {{ … }}.
var.trigger: Trigger variables: {{ trigger.entity }}, {{ trigger.contact }}, {{ trigger.user }}, {{ trigger.eventType }}, {{ trigger.timestamp }}.
var.nodes: Action outputs are namespaced by node id: {{ email.messageId }}, {{ http.response.body }}, {{ ai.text }}, {{ code.tier }}.
var.secrets: Use {{ secrets.MY_TOKEN }} to inject values from Settings → Secrets. Secrets are encrypted at rest and never appear in logs.
var.helpers: Helpers: {{ now() }}, {{ formatDate(date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') }}, {{ upper(text) }}, {{ json(obj) }}, {{ default(value, 'fallback') }}.

kbd.search: Type in the palette search to filter nodes across every category at once.
kbd.results: Matched nodes are highlighted. Hit Enter to grab the first result.
kbd.clear: Press Esc or clear the field to restore the full palette.
kbd.canvas: Canvas shortcuts: Space = pan · scroll = zoom · Cmd/Ctrl+A = select all · Del = delete · Cmd/Ctrl+D = duplicate.
kbd.undoRedo: Cmd/Ctrl+Z = undo · Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z = redo · Cmd/Ctrl+S = save · Cmd/Ctrl+Enter = test run.

concepts.what: A workflow is a recipe your app runs automatically when something happens — for example: 'when an offer is sent, email the customer, wait 2 days, then ask the manager to approve a discount'.
concepts.graph: It's drawn as a graph. Boxes are steps (called nodes), arrows show the order things run in (called edges). The workflow walks from the start, one box at a time.
concepts.trigger: Every workflow starts with a Trigger — the event that wakes it up. A status change, a webhook from another system, a scheduled time, or a manual click.
concepts.actions: Actions are the steps that DO something — send an email, create a record, call an API, run AI, update a status. The bulk of your workflow is actions.
concepts.conditions: Conditions decide which path to take — If/Else for two branches, Switch for many, Loop to repeat per item. They turn a straight line into real business logic.
concepts.variables: Every step exposes its output as a variable. Use {{ trigger.offer.total }} or {{ ai.text }} inside any later step — that's how data flows from one box to the next.
concepts.executions: Each time the trigger fires, a new Execution is created and tracked end-to-end. You can see exactly which step ran, how long it took, the inputs, outputs, retries and errors.
concepts.mental: Mental model: Trigger fires → engine walks the graph → each node reads variables, does its job, writes its own variables → conditions pick the next path → execution ends when all paths finish. That's it.

tb.intro: On the right are the workflow actions, in order: AI builder, Debug, Copy, Import, Export, Groups, Workflows, Test, Cancel/Save and Activate.
tb.test: Test run executes the workflow once on a sample payload — no real emails, no real status changes — and shows you the per-node logs so you can verify the flow before going live.
tb.save: Save commits the current canvas as a new immutable version. Older versions stay around forever — rollback is one click away.
tb.activate: Activate flips the workflow into live mode. From that moment, every real event matching the trigger will fire this workflow.
tb.counter: The counter in the top-left pill shows your progress through the demo — step number out of the total.
tb.status: Top-left you see the live SignalR status — a green pulse means the workflow runtime is connected and ready to receive events.
tb.version: Right next to it sits the version badge. Every Save mints a new version (v1, v2, v3…) — so you can roll back instantly if anything goes wrong.
tb.editPill: The orange "Edit mode" pill warns you that the canvas has unsaved changes. The dot pulses to remind you to Save before leaving.
tb.ai: Build with AI opens an assistant that turns a plain-English description into a complete workflow — nodes, connections, configs and all.
tb.debug: Debug Console streams live executions, lets you inspect every node’s input/output and replay payloads. Indispensable when something misbehaves in production.
tb.copy: Copy Config copies the entire workflow as JSON to your clipboard — handy for pasting into a chat, a ticket or version control.
tb.import: Import lets you paste a workflow JSON to recreate it instantly — great for moving workflows between tenants or environments.
tb.export: Export downloads the workflow as a portable JSON file, including all nodes, edges and node configs.
tb.groups: Workflow Groups let you organise large catalogues of workflows into folders by team, domain or use-case.
tb.manager: The Workflows manager lists every saved workflow on this tenant — open, rename, duplicate, archive or load any of them onto the canvas.
tb.cancel: Cancel discards your unsaved edits and reverts the canvas to the last saved version. It’s your safety net while experimenting.
tb.stop: Once active, Activate becomes Stop. Click it to instantly pause execution without losing the version — perfect for a quick safety break.
